resources.string: Records app file access and personal data queries through Android content providers. Adds Jail (app isolation) controls for Android ID, advertising IDs, app visibility, and file grants.

Big Brother records file reads, location requests and other activity on this device. Adding an app to Jail restricts its access to personal data, gives it separate storage, and blocks access to real device identifiers.
The timeline groups access by hour and app. Open an entry to see what the app accessed.
When you add an app to Jail, supported isolation settings take effect immediately. You can give it separate storage and return an empty clipboard. Each setting can be adjusted individually.
Enable Big Brother in LSPosed or Vector. Keep the recommended scopes, select System Framework, then restart the device.
The Big Brother bodyguard flexes both arms.
Sample timeline showing access by Weather and Flashlight.
Sample Jail settings for Weather with separate storage and an empty clipboard.
Each isolated app receives its own virtual ID.
Apps cannot read the real advertising ID or supported vendor identifiers (OAID).
An app can see only itself and system apps.
Apps can open files picked for the current use. Persisted grants do not apply during isolation.
